narrative:
Your loan application has been reviewed, and unfortunately, the model assessed you as representing a high credit risk, with an 86% predicted probability of defaulting — a figure that led directly to the denial of your application. This decision was shaped by a combination of factors specific to your financial profile, and understanding them may help you take steps toward a more successful application in the future.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, nearly half had no checking account at all, and only about one in five had a negative balance like yours. A negative checking account balance is a strong signal of financial strain, suggesting that day-to-day cash flow may already be under pressure — which raises concerns about your ability to meet regular loan repayments.

The second most important factor was your credit history. While it might seem positive that all your past credits have been paid in full at the bank, this category is actually quite rare among approved applicants — only about 3% of those who were approved share this credit history type. The vast majority of approved applicants either had existing credits they were actively and successfully repaying, or had a history involving critical accounts that were nonetheless resolved. The model appears to interpret "all paid at bank" as a pattern associated with higher risk, possibly because it reflects a very limited or unusual credit track record.

The third significant factor was your property situation. You currently have no registered property or savings-backed assets, which places you in the least favorable property category. Among approved applicants, nearly 87% owned some form of property — whether real estate, a vehicle, or a life insurance policy — providing collateral and a safety net. Having no property means there is little financial cushion to fall back on if repayment difficulties arise.

Beyond these top three factors, a few other aspects of your profile add to the overall picture: your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is higher than the approved applicant average of around 3%, and you have two existing credits at the bank compared to an average of about 1.4 among approved applicants, suggesting your debt obligations are already relatively stretched. You are also supporting two financially dependent people, compared to an average of just over one among approved applicants, which further limits financial flexibility.

As a next step, it would be worth focusing on bringing your checking account into a positive balance and maintaining it there consistently over several months, as this would directly address the most critical concern. Building or registering tangible assets, even modest ones, could also strengthen a future application. Finally, consider speaking with a financial advisor or the bank directly to understand what specific improvements would make the most difference — your loan amount of 1,442 DM is actually well below the approved applicant average of around 2,887 DM, which suggests that with a stronger financial foundation, a future application could be viewed much more favorably.
